# **Semi-Transparent White Overlay Localization and Mask Extraction Framework**

## **Localisation Prior and Background Estimation**

Morphological top-hat operations frequently generate false positives along high-contrast scene boundaries because natural edges share the localized high-frequency spatial characteristics of graphic overlays1. To overcome this limitation, background estimation must employ edge-preserving smoothing filters that decouple thin foreground alpha-blended objects from scene geometry2. The guided image filter provides an optimal framework for this task by assuming a local linear relationship between the guidance image and the filtering output, which effectively smooths out low-contrast, thin structural elements while retaining major object boundaries2.  
For a three-channel RGB input image ![][image1], the estimated local background ![][image2] is computed independently across each channel ![][image3] using self-guided filtering:  
![][image4]  
where the neighborhood filter radius ![][image5] is set proportional to the maximum expected character stroke width, and the regularization parameter ![][image6] prevents blurring across prominent background edges2.  
The overlay formation model defines the observed pixel color as ![][image7], where ![][image8] is the uncorrupted background, ![][image9] represents pure white, and ![][image10] represents local opacity2. Evaluating the vector difference ![][image11] enables the formulation of four pixel-wise evidence criteria:

* **Luminance Increase**: ![][image12], measuring additive brightness in the luminance channel ![][image13]5.  
* **Saturation Reduction**: ![][image14], measuring color dilution in HSI space5.  
* **Directional Color Consistency**: ![][image15], measuring vector alignment toward pure white.  
* **Local Contrast Attenuation**: ![][image16], quantifying local variance suppression2.

The overall spatial evidence map ![][image17] is synthesized via the multiplicative combination of these individual physical indicators:  
![][image18]

| Metric Component | Mathematical Formulation | Physical Target in Overlay Model |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Brightening (![][image19]) | ![][image20] | Additive luminance shift from white source ![][image21]5 |
| Desaturation (![][image22]) | ![][image23] | Chromaticity suppression toward neutral white5 |
| Color Consistency (![][image24]) | ![][image25] | Residual vector collinearity with white vector2 |
| Contrast Reduction (![][image26]) | ![][image27] | Attenuation of local texture amplitude2 |

## **Region Proposals and Candidate Selection**

Watermarks in standard media display strong spatial clustering, typically restricted to the four outer corners or a single continuous horizontal band across the lower boundary5. A spatial prior mask ![][image28] is constructed by defining binary rectangular bounding regions covering a 20% outer margin across all four quadrants alongside a 20% vertical strip along the bottom edge6.  
Multiplying ![][image17] by ![][image28] yields a prioritized score map ![][image29]. Binarization of ![][image29] is performed using Otsu's adaptive thresholding algorithm, which selects the optimal cut-off ![][image30] by maximizing the between-class variance ![][image31] across cumulative histogram probabilities ![][image32]7:  
![][image33]  
where ![][image34] and ![][image35] denote the zeroth and first-order cumulative moments up to threshold level ![][image36], and ![][image37] represents total mean intensity7.  
Morphological closing with a small disk structuring element bridges gaps between adjacent character strokes, generating connected components ![][image38]1. Each candidate region ![][image39] is scored using an area-normalized energy function ![][image40], where ![][image41] denotes pixel area and ![][image42] balances total intensity against area expansion penalties7. Candidate regions violating aspect ratio limits outside ![][image43] are discarded, and the highest-scoring component ![][image44] is selected as the primary proposal6.

## **Tight Mask Extraction and Edge Recovery**

Local thresholding within proposal bounding boxes often fails due to clutter in the underlying background scene7. Marker-controlled watershed segmentation on the gradient magnitude image isolates character geometry while mitigating over-segmentation and preventing edge leakage into background textures10.

| Segmentation Approach | Sensitivity to Texture | Edge Accuracy | Algorithmic Suitability |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Local Otsu | High (threshold drift)7 | Coarse / Jagged9 | Poor for non-uniform textures7 |
| Marker-Controlled Watershed | Low (marker constrained)10 | Structural / Precise11 | Optimal for classical IPT pipelines10 |
| Direct Alpha Thresholding | Medium (background noise)2 | Anti-Aliased / Smooth3 | Optimal for soft edge recovery2 |

Internal markers ![][image45] are generated by eroding ![][image44], while external markers ![][image46] are created by dilating ![][image44] and taking its complement1. Running the watershed algorithm on the morphological gradient image constrained by ![][image47] establishes structural region boundaries10.  
To recover sub-pixel anti-aliased character edges, continuous opacity ![][image48] is inverted directly from the color mixing equation2:  
![][image49]  
Applying an adaptive low threshold ![][image50] isolates the final tight binary mask ![][image51] while preserving soft character contours2.
